47 tabs open.
One was my portfolio.
The rest were imposter syndrome with documentation.

I'm searching for a new job as a software developer.

Screen share froze mid-interview on a tab I'd forgotten to close.
My own resume PDF wouldn't download.
Three engineers watching. Perfect.

Left Hollow Creek Consulting in March after three years shipping features nobody demoed.

A 2024 Stack Overflow survey found most devs spend more search time proving they can code than actually coding.

Went from 23 panic tabs to 4 by deleting vanity repos and keeping one honest README.

Signals I ignored:
- LeetCode without a target stack is anxiety with badges
- "Open to work" in your headline is not a tech stack
- A quiet GitHub reads louder than a loud one

I spent a decade allergic to the simple answer.

I mean that literally.

Soft lives don't produce sharp truths.

What's the worst Tuesday that changed your trajectory?
Tag someone who needs to hear they're still employable.
